articles.headline: Barcelona fan for life -- and beyond: Fans can pay to deposit ashes at Camp Nou
articles.description: Barcelona are giving their fans the possibility to be part of the club once they pass away by offering from 2027 a columbarium and commemorative plaques at their stadium.
articles.body:
Barcelona are giving their fans the possibility to be part of the club once they pass away by offering from 2027 a columbarium and commemorative plaques at their stadium.

As part of the upgrade to Camp Nou, Barça will have a 1,500m² Memorial space consisting of commemorative plaques and 26,000 niches, where fans' ashes can be deposited.

Both the columbarium and commemorative plaques come with concessions lasting for 10, 25 or 50-year periods. Both options are available to Barça fans worldwide as there is no need to be a club member.

"Two ways of paying tribute and showing remembrance will be available through placing a loved one's ashes in a columbarium or writing a name and message on a commemorative plaque in the Stadium. Both options are available to FC Barcelona fans worldwide, there is no need to be a member," a club statement said.

A peaceful resting place at the Camp Nou will cost from €2,490 ($2,762) for a 10-year concession while the 50-year concession will set you back €5,990 ($6,644). In addition, there is a maintenance fee of €70 per year. A standard 10-year plaque is €490 while a 50-year premium one is €1,040.

Designed by architect Quique Montoya, the Memorial space will combine "fine materials, warm lighting and a contemporary style, with large murals dedicated to notable moments in Barça's history, plus visual, audiovisual and sound elements."

The work, which is being carried out in two phases, will be completed in mid-2028.

"Many fans, members and those with a past at the Club have shown interest in the FC Barcelona Memorial since the launch of the project," the club said.

"These include several former players and relatives of historic figures at Barça who have shown their desire to form part of the initiative."

articles.headline: 2026 NFL midseason report: Questions, stats for all 32 teams entering second half
articles.description: The 2026 NFL season has hit the midway point. Here's what to watch in the second half, key QB stats and fantasy nuggets for all 32 teams.
articles.body:
Nine weeks of the 2026 NFL season have passed. Some teams are riding high, while others are grasping for wins.

Much of what we believed we knew when it all began in September has been validated -- but lots of surprises, blockbuster trades and injuries have changed the course of our early-season predictions. 

AFC South-leading Jacksonville went all-in on the defensive side with a trio of trades before the deadline this week, while John Harbaugh has the NFC East-leading New York Giants believing they hired the right man. No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza has yet to take the reins in Las Vegas but will this week after another big trade; there's not a single rookie who has stood out enough so far to say that the race for ROY isn't wide open. The NFC North remains the strongest division halfway through the season, while both Super Bowl participants have looked shaky of late. Of note, neither Seattle (11) nor New England (16) was ranked in the FPI top 10 at this point last season.

With that in mind, ESPN's 32 NFL team reporters took part in a midseason reset. Here, they lay out what they've learned through the first nine games and frame what's to come over the final nine weeks and beyond. Teams are ranked below by where each stands in ESPN's Football Power Index (FPI) rankings, and each club's current odds to win the division are also included as well as Eric Moody's non-QB fantasy football nuggets.

San Francisco 49ers

FPI rank: 1

Chances to make the playoffs: 99.3%

Chances to win their division: 94.6%

First-half storyline: The 49ers have jumped to a 7-1 start despite more injuries to key players, including to DE Nick Bosa (calf) and WR Mike Evans (Achilles tendinitis). But the Niners have again overcome those issues to find themselves in the driver's seat for the NFC's No. 1 seed with wins against three of the last four teams in the 2025 playoffs.

QB stat to know: Brock Purdy leads the NFL with a QBR of 82.5 and is firmly in the mix for the NFL's Most Valuable Player award. Perhaps more important given the other injury issues is that Purdy has started and finished all eight games, providing stability at the game's most important position.

Second-half storyline: Despite the hot start, the 49ers believe they can be better. articles.headline: Fantasy football: Which players can you trust from these backfields-by-committee?
articles.description: Matt Bowen looks at some of the toughest backfields to assess and offers his thoughts going forward.
articles.body:
The lack of quality running back depth has been an issue for fantasy football managers this year, and it's even tougher to find consistent production in the lineup with so many shared backfields across the league.

That got us thinking about how managers can approach teams that are using two backs, as it pertains to setting a weekly lineup (across multiple formats).

Below is a breakdown of 11 running back rooms, placing them in different buckets to give fantasy managers a clear picture of how to value each player moving forward.

One must-start, one streaming option

San Francisco 49ers

Christian McCaffrey (20.8 fantasy PPG) remains a top-five back in fantasy, but don't sleep on rookie Kaelon Black as a flex option in deeper formats. Available in more than 60% of ESPN leagues, Black has seen at least 11 carries in back-to-back games, including a rushing touchdown and three goal-to-go carries in Week 7 versus Atlanta. Plus, we know the 49ers want to manage the workload for McCaffrey. Yes, Black provides very limited receiving upside (three receptions this season), but his running style and pad level jump out, and he plays in the league's best offensive scheme under Kyle Shanahan.

Tampa Bay Buccaneers

In a Tampa offense that has become very run-heavy, Bucky Irving is a locked-in RB1 after scoring 21 or more points in four of his past five games. The tape is really good, too. Fast and elusive with the ball. But with this Bucs offensive identity, should managers look to add and/or play Kenny Gainwell? His numbers are somewhat inflated over the past three games due to the weather in the Carolina game. However, Gainwell has scored at least eight in each game during this stretch, and he had three receptions for 60 yards in Week 9 versus the Bears. Gainwell is available in more than 45% of ESPN leagues, and he fits as a deeper-league pickup who can be used as a flex.

An emerging lead back

Denver Broncos

Jonah Coleman's emergence has created separation from J.K. Dobbins, and with RJ Harvey (knee) on IR we finally have a good read on this running back room. Coleman scored 18.8 points in the Week 9 win over the Panthers, getting 21 touches to Dobbins' five, and finishing with 88 yards from scrimmage and a touchdown. The Broncos have a bye this week, but Coleman, who has 18-plus points in back-to-back games, is the only Denver running back you want in your lineup.

Backfields with multiple starters

Los Angeles Rams

Blake Corum's increased usage (11 or more carries in three straight games) and scoring (11 or more points in five consecutive) has impacted the overall value of Kyren Williams, but both can be played as fantasy starters. Williams, who should still be viewed as a lead runner, has 17 or more touches in his past three games, with a touchdown in two of them. articles.headline: Gary Neville slams Man United's 'classless' handling of Michael Carrick sacking
articles.description: Gary Neville has branded Manchester United "classless" over their actions in the days before Michael Carrick's sacking.
articles.body:
Gary Neville has branded Manchester United "classless" over their actions in the days before Michael Carrick's sacking.

Carrick's departure from the club was finally announced on Thursday morning and Mauricio Pochettino has been lined up to replace him, sources told ESPN.

Official confirmation of Carrick's sacking came after a period of limbo for the former United midfielder, who had reported to Carrington again on Thursday after taking training on Tuesday and Wednesday amid reports he would be removed from his role.

His fate was sealed the day after a meeting took place between the club's powerbrokers in Monaco, where director of football Jason Wilcox and chief executive Omar Berrada travelled to see co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe.

Speaking on the Overlap's Stick to Football podcast, which was recorded prior to Thursday's confirmation, former United defender Neville said the process feels "clumsy."

He said: "We're sat here today recording this programme knowing that Michael Carrick is going to be sacked tomorrow, knowing that they're speaking to Mauricio Pochettino, knowing that they've spoken to [Julian] Nagelsmann, [Eddie] Howe-- and they should be doing that by the way, I'm not saying they shouldn't be doing that.

"But I think the fact they're in Monaco now and they can't sack him today knowing that it's happening, to me it just feels a little bit clumsy, it feels a little bit classless.

"I think if you live in Monaco, you can't leave a guy hanging for 24 or 48 hours just because you live in Monaco, that can't happen."

In May, Carrick was appointed on a permanent basis until 2028 having taken interim charge in January, but the club have struggled so far this term.

United are in the Premier League relegation zone with just eight points having won only one of their 10 league matches this season.

Pochettino has previously managed Tottenham, Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea before becoming United States head coach and Neville praised the Argentinian for the physical fitness instilled within his teams.

"One thing we do know about him is he does run his players, he does put physical fitness really at the top of the agenda. He's always had fit teams, whether they've won or not won," Neville said.

"We used to train at Tottenham's training ground when I was with England and they used to have that Tuesday -- I'm calling it terror Tuesday, but it wasn't called terror Tuesday -- it was called something like that, his run was famous at that time in terms of what he does with every team, he does run them.

"They were always fit his teams, to be fair. That's one thing I think he will deal with straight away, he's obviously got a lot of experience now, he knows how to coach a team."

articles.headline: Michael Carrick sacked by Man United, sources say Mauricio Pochettino close
articles.description: Manchester United have sacked head coach Michael Carrick, the club have confirmed.
articles.body:
Manchester United have sacked head coach Michael Carrick, the club have confirmed.

United are close to an agreement with Mauricio Pochettino and have made contact with the U.S. Soccer Federation as they push forward with plans to hire the former Argentina defender as Carrick's successor, sources have told ESPN.

Carrick leaves Old Trafford with United in the Premier League's relegation zone after just one league win all season.

Carrick met executives Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox at Carrington on Thursday morning -- following a meeting between Berrada, Wilcox and minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe in Monaco on Wednesday -- where he was informed of the decision.

Sources have told ESPN that after heavy back-to-back defeats to Como and Bournemouth last month, club bosses wanted to give Carrick and the players "a further opportunity" to turn things around.

During what has been described as a "comprehensive review," it was decided that during the following three games against Chelsea, Roma and Aston Villa there wasn't enough evidence to suggest the team "was on the right path."

United sources have told ESPN that the decision to sack Carrick has been made because being 18th in the Premier League after 10 games is "not acceptable" and that the squad is "far better than results and performances so far this season have indicated."

There has been criticism about the lack of clarity around Carrick's position and the optics of him leading training sessions on Tuesday and Wednesday amid mounting talk that he was set for the sack. However, club sources have told ESPN that plans for non-international players to train this week were in place more than a month ago.

A club statement said: "Manchester United can confirm that Michael Carrick has departed his role as men's first-team head coach.

"Michael rejoined the club in January and guided the team to a third-placed Premier League finish by winning 12 out of the remaining 17 games of the 2025-26 season, accumulating the highest points tally in the league during that period.

"After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions.

"Michael is, and always will be, a Manchester United legend. Just as he did as a player, he has conducted himself with the highest standards of dedication and professionalism throughout his time back with the club. His leadership and achievements last season will always be fondly remembered.

"The club intends to appoint a permanent successor as quickly as possible."

Carrick was initially handed the job on an interim basis following Ruben Amorim's dismissal in January. He masterminded a surprise 2-0 victory over Manchester City in his first game in charge and went on to win 12 of 17 matches to end the season.

It was enough to finish third in the Premier League and secure a return to the Champions League for the first time since 2023.

articles.headline: Live updates, reaction as Man United sack Michael Carrick as manager
articles.description: Manchester United have sacked manager Michael Carrick after a poor run of results. Follow along for the latest reaction, and speculation over who might replace him.
articles.body:
Michael Carrick has been sacked as Manchester United head coach after the club dropped into the Premier League relegation zone (18th) with just one league win in 10 games (five draws, four losses) -- their worst-ever start to a league season.

A rollercoaster 4-4 draw was saved late at Old Trafford against Aston Villa at the weekend, and came after a 3-2 win from 2-0 down against Roma in the UEFA Champions League in midweek, but it was not enough to save Carrick from the sack.

United States coach Mauricio Pochettino is the favored candidate to replace Carrick, with the United hierarchy -- led by co-chairman Joel Glazer, minority owner Jim Ratcliffe, CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox -- assessing options in the coming days.

Follow along for the latest reaction to the news.

articles.headline: 2026 NFL midseason award rankings: MVP picks, top rookies, OPOY, DPOY, coaches
articles.description: Joe Burrow for MVP? Arvell Reese as the DROY? Hardware for Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Will Anderson Jr.? We ranked the top contenders to win eight NFL awards through Week 9.
articles.body:
It's midseason awards time. I'm here to hand out my ballot for the first half of the 2026 NFL season. And in a year that has felt dominated by parity and very few players or teams separating from the pack, it wasn't easy to pick favorites. There are multiple legitimate contenders to win every single award through nine weeks, running all the way from Most Valuable Player (where I counted six players who had a legitimate argument) to Comeback Player of the Year (where three future Hall of Famers came back from season-ending injuries and immediately looked like their old selves).

Subscribe: 'The Bill Barnwell Show'

As always, these are my picks for who I feel should win each of these awards after the first half of the season as opposed to predictions for who the voters are likely to actually select by the end of the year. I place a priority on availability, so players who have sat out more than a game or so because of injury will find it difficult to compete with players who have answered the call each and every weekend. And naturally, I'm using healthy amounts of data and what I've seen watching All-22 film every week to inform my choices here.

Let's begin with the rookies before wrapping with my MVP rankings and my midseason All-Pro team.

Jump to an award:

DROY | OROY | Coach of the Year

Comeback Player of the Year

Protector of the Year

DPOY | OPOY | MVP | All-Pro roster

Defensive Rookie of the Year

My top pick five weeks ago: Arvell Reese

After the offense-heavy draft classes in 2024 and 2025, this has been a very fun crop of defensive rookies, driven by the players at the very top. There were no sure things, but we're seeing a lot of players who had questions about their fit in a defense or as every-down options thrive. The 49ers and Chiefs first-year defenders in particular have been exciting to watch, although Mansoor Delane's shoulder injury has kept the top-drafted cornerback in the class from getting on the field often enough to compete for this award, while defensive tackle Gracen Halton sustained a season-ending broken ankle for the 49ers.

I was left with five contenders for three spots. Jacob Rodriguez has been ever present at linebacker for the Dolphins and has been a very good run defender while wearing the green dot for Miami as a rookie. The Bengals were able to isolate Rodriguez in coverage for a couple of touchdowns earlier this season, but he has generally had the athleticism to compete there against running backs and tight ends.

And though Brandon Cisse's season got off to a tough start against Justin Jefferson, the Packers cornerback has improved. He has been surprisingly impactful along the line of scrimmage, creating problems as a blitzer and making quick reads and sure tackles on screens. He has been one of the biggest reasons why the Packers -- whose outside cornerbacks struggled last season -- have been able to withstand the absence of Micah Parsons.

articles.headline: Why 2-7 Jets preferred to keep roster intact at trade deadline
articles.description: A year after making two blockbuster trades, New York stayed quiet at the NFL trade deadline.
articles.body:
FLORHAM PARK, N.J. -- One year after rocking the NFL with the Sauce Gardner and Quinnen Williams blockbusters at the trade deadline, the New York Jets made no splashy deals despite obvious roster needs and a handful of players that would've fetched nice returns.

Ahead of Tuesday's deadline, general manager Darren Mougey was quiet -- well, except for a minor trade involving backup safety Andre Cisco, who was sent to the Detroit Lions for a 2029 sixth-round pick.

The Jets were only interested in trading players on expiring contracts (like Cisco), preferring to keep their 2027 roster intact. While some might argue that a team with 21 losses in its last 26 games should've reached for the sun and moon to improve its future, the Jets sent three messages by standing (almost) pat:

They like their foundation.

They already have enough draft capital (three first-round picks in 2027).

They want to give embattled coach Aaron Glenn a chance to develop the current roster.

Plus, let's be honest, there also was a subliminal message: With Glenn on the hot seat, they wanted to wait until the coaching dust settles in the offseason before selling off players that might intrigue a new coaching staff.

Explaining their approach to the deadline, Glenn said Wednesday, "[Our] philosophy hasn't changed from last year."

He said they will always listen to inquiries, but "we won't force any issues, and we'll make sure we do what's best for the organization."

Glenn likes the current roster, claiming, "We're right on the cusp of trying to break through."

He noted that the Jets have lost five one-score games against a tough schedule. In fact, they're 1-5 in one-score games, 4-10 in two seasons under Glenn. Based on their opponents' records, the Jets' strength of schedule ranks 23rd, per ESPN Analytics.

Some might argue, "So close, yet so far."

A look at why the Jets retained certain players and what it means for their future:

Quarterback Geno Smith: Smith fit the expiring-contract criterion, but they never entertained the idea of moving him despite pre-deadline buzz with the Minnesota Vikings. The Jets don't have an experienced backup, so trading Smith would've been tantamount to surrendering the season and ending Glenn. The No. 2 is rookie Cade Klubnik, a fourth-round pick who has yet to take a snap.

At 2-7, the season is basically lost, but a downgrade at quarterback would've hampered their ability to develop young players such as wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. and tight ends Mason Taylor and Kenyon Sadiq. At this point, player development is paramount. Smith, ranked 19th in QBR, can keep the offense operating at a functional level.

Smith, who said he paid no attention to the speculation, also could fit into their 2027 plan as a stopgap starter/mentor for a highly-drafted rookie.

articles.headline: How Kobe, LeBron, Steph and Brady are helping Jayden Daniels chase greatness
articles.description: The Commanders QB has tapped into some of sports' all-time greats like Brady and LeBron in search of an edge.
articles.body:
ASHBURN, Va. -- Shortly after midnight in the wake of Washington's Week 8 win over the Philadelphia Eagles, quarterback Jayden Daniels exited his news conference and channeled one of his idols. Instead of driving home, Daniels took an hours detour to the Commanders' practice facility.

He had more work to do.

For approximately two and a half hours, Daniels worked in near silence. He lifted weights under the guidance of strength and conditioning coach Chad Englehart. The only sounds in the building came from the two men: their conversation and the clanking of weights.

Daniels, who grew up as a massive Kobe Bryant fan, is well aware the Los Angeles Lakers legend used to work out at 4 a.m., hours before anyone else arrived. It was part of the "Mamba Mentality," a phrase based on Bryant's Black Mamba nickname. And now, Daniels has adopted similar habits in his quest to tap into his potential.

"It's just the work ethic and the obsession to want to be better and obviously wanting to win," Daniels said. "As I got to learn more about the Mamba Mentality ... Kobe is a huge inspiration for me. You do whatever it takes to win."

That includes talking to as many people as possible about how they succeeded, picking up tips along the way. Daniels has done so since entering the NFL as the No. 2 pick in 2024. He says it is not about trying to insert himself into the circles of famous people. It's about learning what made them great, or how they overcame injuries, scrutiny and adversity early in their careers -- situations with which Daniels has experience.

In Washington, he leaned on Super Bowl winner and future Hall of Fame linebacker Bobby Wagner in their two seasons together. He has tapped into Hall of Fame quarterbacks Tom Brady, Drew Brees, Peyton Manning and reigning MVP Matthew Stafford. He has taken advantage of his wider profile in the sports world, establishing relationships with players such as LeBron James, Steph Curry and Draymond Green among others. He has also picked the brain of Lakers executive Rob Pelinka, Bryant's former agent, and he routinely talks to Commanders advisor Bob Myers, the architect behind the Golden State Warriors' basketball dynasty.

"All the great ones have overcome adversity at some point," Daniels said. "Everybody has to deal with it. It's good to just hear a perspective of how other people dealt with it."

Daniels' adversity included dealing with multiple injuries, questionable in-game decisions that proved costly and even a flap about not wanting LSU to reassign his No. 5, which Daniels thought had been retired.

What he learned from them all: Bury yourself in the work.

That's why, after the Week 8 weight-lifting session that lasted into the wee hours, Daniels stuck around to watch film of the 27-10 win over the Eagles while it was still fresh in his mind before finally heading home around 3:30 a.m.

articles.headline: Does Packers' Christian Watson + Matthew Golden = 3,000 yards?
articles.description: Watson and Golden are on pace to join a rare club of WR pairs who combined for 3,000 yards.
articles.body:
GREEN BAY, Wis. -- No one is more relieved about the emergence of receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden than the Green Bay Packers' custodial department.

They no longer have to worry about cleaning up after a potential disgorgement.

Those in charge of keeping Lambeau Field neat and tidy have been on call for the better part of the past two years -- ever since coach Matt LaFleur grew tired of being asked whether they'll ever find a No. 1 receiver again and quipped: "I want to vomit every time I hear 'number one wide receiver' to be honest with you."

Halfway through this season, there is little question that the Packers have a WR1(a) and WR2(b) pair with Watson and Golden, who have transformed Green Bay's offense into one of the most explosive in the league despite the absence of any semblance of a running game.

Through nine games, Watson and Golden rank third and fourth, respectively, in the NFL in receiving yards. If they keep this up, they will write themselves into the record books as one of the most productive receiving tandems in NFL history.

Watson's 879 yards receiving puts him on pace for 1,660 yards. Golden's 783 calculates to 1,479 yards over the 17-game regular season. Combined, that's 3,139 yards.

There have been only four pairs of teammates who combined for 3,000 receiving yards in a single season, according to Elias Sports Bureau. The most was a 3,174-yard season by the Lions duo of Brett Perriman (1,488 yards) and Herman Moore (1,686 yards) in 1995, and that was in a 16-game season.

And there has never been a team with a pair of 1,500-yard receivers.

The Packers went from not having a reliable No. 1 receiver since Davante Adams' departure after the 2021 season, which was the last time they had a 1,000-yard receiver, to seemingly having two of them.

"The numbers they're putting up, the plays they're making, yeah, I feel like we've got two number ones for sure," Packers offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich said this week. "But again, we don't look at it that way. We look at it as you got two great players, how can we just get them the ball, and it's a great problem to have."

It's exactly what LaFleur and general manager Brian Gutekunst envisioned when they streamlined their receiver room in the offseason. After they let Romeo Doubs leave in free agency and traded Dontayvion Wicks, they acknowledged it was more challenging than they thought to keep so many receivers happy last season.

Sunday's win over the New England Patriots validated their thinking. With Jordan Love pinpointing deep ball after deep ball, Watson and Golden had massive -- and nearly perfect -- performances. Between the two of them, they caught 17 of 18 targets. The only missed connection was a sideline pass that was just off the outstretched hand of Watson, which would've added another 35 yards or so to his total. articles.descriptionJa: バイエルン・ミュンヘンは、リヴァプールのウィング、リオ・ングモハを獲得することで攻撃陣の補強を狙っている。最新の移籍情報はTransfer Talkが伝えている。
articles.body:
Bayern Munich are still in talks to sign Liverpool's teenage winger Rio Ngumoha, while Manchester United's list of defensive options now includes Brentford center back Nathan Collins, while Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Bayern Munich are still in talks to sign Liverpool's teenage winger Rio Ngumoha, as reported by Bild's Christian Falk. Bayern were willing to pay €70 million to land the 18-year-old during the summer as they looked for a left winger who could complement Luis Díaz, before they went on to sign Ismael Saibari. But Bayern still need a left winger and could still look to land the England international in either January or the summer transfer window.

- Brentford center back Nathan Collins has been added to Manchester United's list of defensive options for the January transfer window, as reported by The Daily Mail. The Republic of Ireland captain has a contract until 2029, but 8th-placed Brentford would expect a hefty sum to let him go. Only Crystal Palace and Ipswich Town have conceded more Premier League goals this season than the 19 Man United have let in, and Fulham defender Calvin Bassey is also reported to be on the club's shortlist.

- Arsenal are eyeing a January move for Real Madrid forward Endrick, according to TalkSPORT. The versatile 20-year-old has played just 114 minutes this season and the Gunners are looking for attacking reinforcements on the wing following Bukayo Saka's injury. The Brazil international is one of a number of options being offered to Premier League clubs, but Diario AS has suggested there will be competition from AS Roma and Sporting CP, who both want to take Endrick on loan.

- In addition to referencing Endrick, The Independent has suggested Arsenal are also looking at Atlético Madrid's Álex Baena, RB Leipzig's Antonio Nusa and AFC Bournemouth's Junior Kroupi as they aim to sign a winger. With Real Madrid, Atlético and Chelsea all interested in central midfielder Martín Zubimendi, the Gunners would use the funds from any departure to sign a wide man.
